Few American towns are as charming and haunted.
Founded on Georgia's coast in 1733,
this sultry southern bell lies beneath miles of old Spanish moss
and on top of its original burial grounds.
Yep, Savannah is literally built on its own dead.
From early settlers to slaves and all the way up through the Civil War,
by day Savannah's filled with tourists wandering its cobblestone streets.
But when the sun goes down,
that's when the spookies come out.
For hundreds of years now, locals have been seeing everything from ghostly apparitions
in the trees
to a statue that cries tears of blood.
And the paranormal epicenter of it all,
Wright Square.
Wright Square is also known as the Hanging Square.
The original courthouse,
the gallows, and the cemetery were all side by side.
So you could try 'em, hang 'em, and bury 'em all within 100 yd or so.

disembodied voices, and even the spirit of a desperate young mother still searching for her baby.
